comment: Gives great feedback, and I learned so much! Very energetic and supportive prof if you seek her out

Professor Bertucci is nice and accessible outside of class. Her class demands a lot of work with different projects spread out throughout the semester. She also demands a lot of participation. Her instructions are sometimes unclear. She tries to be enthusiastic in class but at times it could be too much. But you do learn a lot about film.

Sonja is quite possibly the best professor on campus. Not only is she great at helping her students learn the art of filmmaking, but she also knows when to be supportive and when to be critical. You'll do a lot of hard work in her class, but in the end it will be well worth your time. If you're at all interested in film, take Sonja's classes.

I enjoyed Sonjas 202 class so much that I took 302 right after. Shes one of the most passionate and creative people Ive met, and she really cares about her students. Her classes are a lot of work, especially during projects (an editing project, a screenplay, and a short film). But none of it feels like work-- she makes the whole process fun.

I thought this was a super hard class when I took it, but even though it took me a while, I realized most of what I hoped to know. Dr. Bertucci knows what she is talking about, even if she is hard, it is in your best interest to listen. You won't soon forget what you learn in this class.

if you're thinking about taking her, do it. she's actually not a tough grader- sometimes the work required for a class like this can seem like a lot but its actually pretty standard for a film class, and she grades fairly. she thinks of her students beyond the classroom and is so caring. whether she knows it or not, shes made my bad days better.

i love sonja!! she's literally the best and most caring professor ever. film is such a fun class to take and she makes it so much more enjoyable. shes super energetic and keeps class interesting. always there to help, even wrote me an RA recommendation when i needed one :)

I took FMST202 after I couldn't get in to FMST101 and I'm glad that I did. There is a lot of work involved so don't expect to just make dumb videos and get an A. She is brilliant, extremely knowledgeable in her field and has high standards but you will learn so much. There's a lot of work outside of class (making films) but it's really rewarding.
